_readme: Every setting the site needs at build time. Edit this file, run `node build.js`, upload. Nothing else needs touching to go live.
_origin: REQUIRED before running ads. The public https origin, no trailing slash — e.g. https://visalavida.es. It builds the canonical links, the sitemap and the absolute og:image URLs Meta's crawler needs for link previews. The build refuses to mark itself production-ready while this is example.com.

integrations._leadEndpoint: STRONGLY RECOMMENDED. A URL that accepts POST application/json and hands the lead to wherever you actually read it (CRM, Google Sheet, Telegram bot, email). A Make/Zapier/n8n webhook works. Whatever you use must answer with CORS header Access-Control-Allow-Origin for this origin, and must return 2xx — the page treats a non-2xx as a failed lead and tells the visitor so.
integrations._formsubmitEmail: Backup sink via formsubmit.co, no server required. ACTIVATION IS MANDATORY: submit the form once yourself after the first deploy, open the confirmation email formsubmit.co sends to this address, click the link. Until you do, formsubmit accepts posts and delivers nothing. Leave empty to disable.
integrations._capiWebhook: Optional. Your relay to the Meta Conversions API. The page posts a ready CAPI payload (phone and name already SHA-256 hashed, event_id matching the browser pixel so Meta deduplicates). Your relay only has to add the access token and forward to graph.facebook.com.
integrations._metaDomainVerification: Optional. The content value from Events Manager -> Settings -> Domain verification -> Meta-tag method. Needed to control your own link edits and to run Aggregated Event Measurement on iOS traffic.
integrations._geoCountryUrl: Optional. URL returning the visitor's country, used to prefill the phone field's dialling code. Set it to "/cdn-cgi/trace" if the site is behind Cloudflare — that answers from your own domain, so no third party sees the visitor and there is no rate limit. Any endpoint of yours returning {"country_code":"ES"} works too. Leave empty and the code is resolved via the public ipwho.is service, falling back to the browser timezone.
integrations._consentMode: 'eu' = the pixel is initialised with consent revoked and sends nothing until the visitor accepts the banner (what GDPR requires for EU/Spain traffic). 'off' = no banner, the pixel tracks from the first paint. Only choose 'off' if you are certain none of your audience is in the EU/UK.

_videoId: YouTube id shown on the thank-you page. Loaded only after the visitor clicks play.

legal._operator: Shown in the privacy policy as the party responsible for the personal data. Replace with the registered company name and address before running ads — Meta reviewers and EU visitors both check this page.
